title: Liquid ETF Trend Defense
market_niche: Highly liquid broad-market ETFs with slow-moving institutional allocation flows.
phenomenon: Large risk-off regimes can persist long enough that slow trend filters may reduce severe drawdowns.
counterparty_or_forced_actor: Benchmark-constrained allocators, retirement flows, and systematic risk-budget reductions that react slowly to changing regimes.
why_edge_might_exist: Broad risk regimes often persist because allocators, risk models, and mandates adjust gradually instead of instantly.
why_large_funds_might_ignore_it: The idea is easy to know, crowded, tax-inefficient for some accounts, benchmark-drifting, and unattractive when judged against full-cycle equity beta.

institutional_constraint_evidence.estimated_position_size: small personal accounts through multi-million-dollar liquid ETF allocations
institutional_constraint_evidence.estimated_strategy_capacity: high in SPY, but expected edge after costs is likely small and crowded
institutional_constraint_evidence.number_of_opportunities_per_year: few major regime changes plus repeated whipsaws

expected_capacity: High for execution, lower for excess edge because the mechanism is widely known.
execution_constraints: daily close signal with next-open fill
consistent adjusted OHLC and benchmark treatment
persistence_mechanism: Slow allocation, risk-management, and behavioral responses can make major equity regimes persistent.
crowding_risk: High, because moving-average timing is simple and widely published.
edge_decay_trigger: Repeated failure to reduce drawdown across multiple equity bear markets after realistic costs and adjusted-price audits.
observable_prediction: Trend-defense rules should lower max drawdown materially while retaining a prespecified fraction of buy-and-hold CAGR.
falsification_tests: Reject the exact strategy hypothesis if CAGR retention and drawdown-reduction thresholds are not both met.
Weaken the thesis if date-window sensitivity shows drawdown improvement only in one cherry-picked period.
Treat measurement as invalid if adjusted-price or benchmark economics are inconsistent.
suggested_validation: Use one prespecified trend length before running.
Separate research-system validity from strategy-hypothesis status.
Run cost, date, and train/test validation before accepting the hypothesis.
references: Hurst, Ooi, and Pedersen, A Century of Evidence on Trend-Following Investing
Moskowitz, Ooi, and Pedersen, Time Series Momentum
